docs.title: Paladio Documentation Portal
docs.text:
Welcome to the technical documentation portal for Paladio, a 100% sovereign, air-gappable travel intelligence and combinatorial optimization platform.

Paladio bridges the gap between conversational generative AI and provable mathematical optimization, orchestrating multi-agent state machines, continuous semantic taste learning, and sub-millisecond C++ combinatorial routing on local hardware.

docs.title: 🏛️ The Three Architectural Tenets
docs.text:
graph LR
    subgraph Tenet1 [1. Total Sovereignty]
        A[Zero Cloud APIs]
        B[Local Quantized LLMs]
        C[Air-Gap Ready]
    end
    subgraph Tenet2 [2. Mathematical Rigor]
        D[Compiled C++20 Solver]
        E[TCOPTW Formulation]

    end
    subgraph Tenet3 [3. Adaptive Learning]
        G[768-D Semantic Hypersphere]

  1. Absolute Data Sovereignty: Zero cloud dependencies. No OpenAI, Anthropic, or proprietary mapping API subscriptions. The entire stack (language models, vector databases, routing engines) runs locally inside standard Docker containers.
  2. Deterministic Mathematical Rigor: Large Language Models are never trusted with arithmetic, routing, or combinatorial search. LLMs perform NLP extraction; all mathematical optimization is solved by a dedicated, compiled C++20 engine (paladio-core).
  3. Continuous Taste Adaptation: A 768-dimensional latent vector space continuously adapts to shifting user tastes using Exponential Moving Averages (EMA), projecting latent embeddings into 8 human-interpretable categories for live frontend telemetry.

docs.title: Paladio Trip Wallet
docs.text: Sovereign, air-gappable digital wallet and credential vault for Paladio trips. Manages boarding passes, lodging access codes, museum/attraction passes, rail/transit tickets, and custom vouchers.

docs.title: Phase 0: Recon & Engineering Conventions
docs.text:
The Trip Wallet strictly aligns with established Paladio patterns:

  1. Frontend Architecture & Data Fetching:
  2. HTTP Client: apiFetch<T> in frontend/src/utils/api.ts with error handling, authentication bearer forwarding, and AbortSignal support.
  3. Toasts: Zustand notification store useNotificationStore.getState().addNotification(...).
  4. Modals: Accessible shared modal Modal.tsx.
  5. Icons: Native inline SVG components in frontend/src/components/icons.tsx (TicketIcon, PlaneIcon, RefreshIcon, Spinner, etc.).
  6. Styling: Native CSS variables (--color-bg-main, --color-surface-card, --color-accent-primary, --color-border, etc.) adhering to the aerospace/brutalist monospace-forward aesthetic with // COMMENT_SECTION headers.

  7. Formatting: Standardized Intl.DateTimeFormat with timezone-aware airport/city conversion instead of raw ISO timestamps.

  8. Backend Architecture & Security:

  9. Web Framework: FastAPI async endpoints with Pydantic v2 schemas and Dependency Injection.
  10. ORM & Persistence: SQLAlchemy 2.0 AsyncSession with PostgreSQL 16 JSONB and timezone-aware DateTime(timezone=True).
  11. Migrations: Alembic auto-generation and explicit schema contracts.
  12. Encryption at Rest: Application-level AES-128-CBC / HMAC-SHA256 via cryptography.fernet.Fernet (WALLET_ENCRYPTION_KEY). Secrets (door codes, raw barcode strings, Wi-Fi credentials) are encrypted before writing to database columns.
  13. Authorization: Strict trip membership validation and creator isolation for private tickets to prevent IDOR vulnerabilities.

  14. Parsing: Deterministic IATA BCBP parser, zxing-cpp for barcode symbologies (PDF417, Aztec, QR, Code128), and pypdf for text extraction. All parsing runs locally with zero external network requests.

  15. Storage & Volumes:

  16. Attachments stored on disk under WALLET_STORAGE_DIR (defaults to /data/wallet_attachments or local app storage), tracked in trip_ticket_attachments.

docs.title: Paladio Deal Engine: Architectural Decisions (D1 - D8)
docs.text: Record of foundational decisions made prior to Deal Engine implementation, adhering to the Sovereign and Air-gappable architecture.

docs.title: D1: Flight Price Source for Tier 1 Discovery & Live Quotes
docs.text:
• Answer: Ryanair public live fare finder API (https://www.ryanair.com/api/farfnd/v4/oneWayFares and roundTripFares) for European routes.
  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Who Decided: Human Owner & Implementing Principal Architect.
  • Evidence: Open unauthenticated JSON endpoints returning real live flight prices in EUR, departure and arrival UTC/local times, IATA codes, carrier details, and exact booking deep-links. Zero API keys, zero credential leaks, rate-limit friendly with client-side exponential backoff.
  • Open Questions: None. Confirmed working via live curl testing for MAD, FCO, OPO, LIS, BCN, DUB, LON.

docs.title: D2: Lodging Price Source & Summary Construction
docs.text:
• Answer: Destination summary built from sampled properties per city across quality tiers (Hostel, Budget, Standard).
  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Who Decided: Human Owner & Implementing Principal Architect (using PLAN.md suggested default).
  • Evidence: Destination-level statistics (stat = median or min, with sample_n recorded) allow like-for-like baseline comparisons without per-hotel lock-in. Nightly base rates plus estimated fee ratios model landed costs.
  • Open Questions: None.

docs.title: D3: Legal / Approved Sources for Scraping / Queries
docs.text:
• Answer: Only public open endpoints and open directories with no API keys or login credentials. No scraping of sources not explicitly approved.
  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Who Decided: Human Owner & Implementing Principal Architect.
  • Evidence: Standard HTTP JSON requests to public fare finder APIs avoid bot detection, CAPTCHAs, and legal ToS friction.
  • Open Questions: None.

docs.title: D4: Historical Dataset for Baselines
docs.text:
• Answer: Build own history through Phase 2 continuous ingestion and the cold-start fallback plan.
  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Who Decided: PLAN.md suggested default confirmed by Human Owner.
  • Evidence: Avoids stale or license-tainted third-party commercial dumps. Route baselines fall back gracefully (full -> drop_lead -> drop_month) when samples are below MIN_BASELINE_ROWS.
  • Open Questions: None.

docs.title: D5: Scale in 6 Months
docs.text:
• Answer: 5,000 active alerts, 100 destinations, 30 origins, 1,000 users.
  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Who Decided: PLAN.md suggested default confirmed by Human Owner.
  • Evidence: TimescaleDB hypertable chunk interval of 3 days with compression after 7 days scales easily to millions of raw ticks without degrading query latency.
  • Open Questions: None.

docs.title: Explanation: Agent Safety & Sovereign Security Model
Core Philosophy: The Sovereign Guardrail
docs.text:
Paladio's Trip Agent operates in a personal, self-hosted, multi-traveler environment. Because LLMs are non-deterministic and susceptible to prompt injection or hallucination, Paladio enforces an architectural safety perimeter:

The Model Proposes; The C++ Engine & User Validate. 1. LLMs are strictly restricted to semantic classification and parameter extraction. Combinatorial optimization, schedule feasibility, and distance calculations are executed deterministically in C++20 (paladio_core). 2. No mutation is committed without passing database authorization checks, Pydantic model validation, and optimistic revision locks.

docs.title: 1. Multi-Tier Permission Hierarchy
docs.text:
Tools are partitioned into three immutable security tiers:

graph TD
    Prompt[User Input / Prompt] --> Intent[Intent & Argument Extraction]
    Intent --> TierCheck{Tool Tier}
    TierCheck -->|Tier A: Read-Only| ExecA[Immediate Execution]
    TierCheck -->|Tier B: Reversible Mutation| ExecB[Execute & Generate Undo Snapshot]
    TierCheck -->|Tier C: Destructive/Cost| PropC[Generate Proposal & Await User Click]
    PropC -->|User Approves| ExecB
    PropC -->|User Rejects / Timeout| Abort[Discard Proposal]

docs.title: Tier A (Query / Read-Only)
docs.text:
• Pure queries with zero write operations (get_trip_overview, get_itinerary, list_expenses).
  • Enforces TripAccessLevel.VIEWER.

docs.title: Tier B (Direct Reversible Mutation)
docs.text:
• Add, move, or re-sequence waypoints within existing days.
  • Every mutation records a complete snapshot in trip_revisions and generates a reversible undo_token.
  • Enforces TripAccessLevel.EDITOR.

docs.title: Tier C (Destructive / Cost / Rebalance)
docs.text:
• Actions that delete entire days, rebalance multi-day itineraries, or finalize payments.
  • Blocked from automatic execution by the model. The server returns a ProposalData structure with a strict TTL (typically 5 minutes).
  • Changes are only applied when the user explicitly clicks Approve in the client interface, transmitting the cryptographically unforgeable proposal ID back over the WebSocket.

docs.title: 2. Optimistic Concurrency & Revision Control
docs.text:
To prevent race conditions between collaborating users and agent turns: 1. Every trip has an integer revision column. 2. Every mutation executes a Compare-And-Swap (CAS) update: 

UPDATE trips
SET itinerary_data = :new_data, revision = revision + 1
WHERE id = :trip_id AND revision = :expected_revision;
3. If concurrent edits occur, the update fails with 409 Conflict, triggering an automatic re-fetch rather than silently overwriting user work.

docs.title: 3. Defense Against Prompt Injection & IDOR
docs.text:
1. In-Process Access Verification: Every tool invocation validates the user's role on the specific trip_id. An attacker cannot prompt the agent to read or modify another user's trip because all SQL queries are scoped to the authenticated traveler's access matrix.
  2. Secret Redaction: Passwords, ticket barcodes, and access PINs are masked at the service boundary (mask_secret()), ensuring raw secrets never enter the LLM context window where they could be leaked.
  3. No Self-Approval: Proposals are stored in Redis with UUID keys. The model cannot pass confirmed=True for a Tier C tool on its own; confirmation tokens are only accepted when signed by the user's client session.

docs.title: 4. Comprehensive Audit Trail
docs.text:
Every MCP action is written to the agent_actions table: - timestamp, tool, outcome (success / failure / rejected) - user_id and trip_id - JSON payload of exact input arguments - Resulting database revision number

This guarantees 100% post-facto auditability for all automated and semi-automated itinerary changes.

docs.title: Architectural Explanation: Continuous-to-Discrete Harmonics
docs.text:
One of Paladio's unique technical innovations is its mathematical bridging of continuous latent embeddings and discrete human-interpretable category radar telemetry.

This document outlines the geometric theory behind the 8-D Harmonic Projection.

docs.title: 1. The Interpretability Gap in Latent Spaces
docs.text:
While dense 768-D vector embeddings excel at mathematical similarity computations, they suffer from the interpretability gap: a vector \(\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^{768}\) is completely opaque to a human traveler.

Travelers do not think in continuous 768-dimensional coordinates; they think in tangible interests: - "I enjoy historical landmarks and fine food, but I don't care for nightlife."

To provide transparent, explainable recommendations, Paladio projects continuous latent trajectories onto an 8-dimensional harmonic basis.

docs.title: 2. Defining the Canonical Anchor Hypersphere
docs.text:
In backend/app/engine/scoring/semantic_learning.py, 8 canonical travel categories are defined by descriptive natural language prompts:

1. art_culture        (Fine arts, museums, exhibitions, sculptures)
2. history_heritage   (Monuments, castles, cathedrals, archaeology)
3. nature_outdoors    (Parks, botanical gardens, lakes, trails)
4. architecture       (Urban facades, towers, bridges, city design)
5. food_culinary      (Gastronomy, tapas, local dining, bistros)
6. nightlife          (Cocktail bars, speakeasies, music venues)
7. shopping           (Artisan markets, boutiques, antique stores)
8. scenic_views       (Miradors, rooftop viewpoints, observation decks)

At module initialization, each anchor prompt is embedded into a 768-D vector and normalized to unit length:

\[\mathbf{u}_k = \frac{\text{Embed}(P_k)}{\|\text{Embed}(P_k)\|_2} \quad \text{for } k \in [1, \dots, 8]\]

These 8 vectors act as anchor poles defining an 8-dimensional basis on the 768-D unit hypersphere \(\mathbb{S}^{767}\).

docs.title: 3. The Harmonic Projection Mapping
docs.text:
Given a user's latent preference vector \(\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{767}\) (which continuously adapts via EMA on every conversational turn), its projection onto category \(k\) is calculated by:

\[\mathbf{a}_k = \text{clip}\left(\frac{\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{u}_k + 1}{2}, \, 0.0, \, 1.0\right)\]

Because both \(\mathbf{v}\) and \(\mathbf{u}_k\) are unit vectors, their inner product \(\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{u}_k \equiv \cos(\theta)\) is strictly bounded in \([-1.0, 1.0]\): - If \(\cos(\theta) = 1.0\) (perfect alignment): \(\mathbf{a}_k = 1.0\). - If \(\cos(\theta) = 0.0\) (orthogonal / neutral): \(\mathbf{a}_k = 0.5\). - If \(\cos(\theta) = -1.0\) (diametrically opposed): \(\mathbf{a}_k = 0.0\).

docs.title: 4. Driving Real-Time UI Radar Telemetry
docs.text:
The resulting vector \(\mathbf{a} \in [0, 1]^8\) is transmitted directly over WebSockets to the Next.js frontend:

graph LR
    P[User Prompt] -->|OnnxEmbeddingProvider fastembed| V[768-D Vector]
    V -->|EMA Update| U[Permanent User Vector]
    U -->|Harmonic Projection| A[8-D Vector]
    A -->|WebSocket /ws/stream| R[SVG PreferenceRadar Component]

This transforms complex multi-dimensional machine learning into an intuitive, interactive radar polygon that updates in real time as the user chats with the AI swarm.

docs.title: 1. Executive Overview & System Topology
docs.text:
The Paladio Market Deal Engine is designed as a continuous, sovereign ingestion pipeline that discovers anomalous travel deals (flights and hotels) across user-monitored corridors without relying on paid commercial SaaS aggregators.

The pipeline comprises two parallel intake vectors: 1. Flight Ingestion Vector: Gathers scheduled and dynamic flight quotes across intra-Europe, intra-Americas, and intercontinental corridors. 2. Lodging Ingestion Vector: Gathers live hotel, hostel, and apartment availability, night rates, star ratings, and review distributions for destination municipalities.

These vectors feed into a TimescaleDB time-series hypertable (market_price_ticks), aggregate into daily rollups (price_daily), calculate empirical price distributions (route_baselines), and execute a 6-stage detection funnel to notify users of high-confidence, bookable vacation packages.

docs.title: 2. Triggering & Orchestration Subsystem
docs.text: Ingestion tasks are coordinated through asynchronous Celery workers, a dedicated Celery Beat scheduler, and FastAPI REST endpoints.

docs.title: 2.1 Daily Scheduled Pipeline (backend/app/tasks.py)
docs.text:
1. daily_market_pipeline_task (tasks.py):
  2. Schedule: Executes daily at 03:00 UTC via Celery Beat (beat_schedule: crontab(hour=3, minute=0)).
  3. Concurrency Control: Protected by a non-blocking Redis distributed lock (paladio:market:daily_chain_lock, TTL 2 hours) ensuring overlapping daily runs are strictly impossible.

  4. Pipeline Chain:

    1. Stage 1 (Sweep): Calls run_daily_flight_sweep, sweeping all watched alert corridors and pilot routes across the 11-month forward calendar horizon with per-route fault isolation. Records audit rows in market_sweep_runs and route_month_coverage.
    2. Stage 2 (Baselines): Calls compute_route_baselines, recomputing statistical medians, quantiles, and fee models across 6 lead buckets for each route.
    3. Stage 3 (Detection & Verification & Hotels): Calls run_deal_detection_scan, selecting top-3 candidates per user per day with route diversity capping (MAX_PER_ROUTE_PER_SCAN = 2), performing live tolerance verification, and fetching authentic lodging only for verified candidates.

  5. backfill_route_corpus_task (tasks.py):

  6. Schedule: On-demand or triggered during initial route setup.

  7. Behavior: Calls backfill_route_corpus, sweeping forward calendar months up to CORPUS_HORIZON_MONTHS = 11 (330 days) to populate authentic market prices and establish route baselines.

  8. prewarm_route_lodging_task (tasks.py:L2225):

  9. Schedule: Triggered post-flight backfill.
  10. Behavior: Sweeps 4-night lodging stays across representative weekends in the forward horizon to populate baseline lodging costs.

docs.title: 2.2 On-Demand REST API Endpoints (backend/app/api/market.py)
docs.text:
• POST /api/market/routes/{route_id}/scan (market.py:L950): Manually triggers a live scan for a specific route alert.
  • POST /api/market/routes/{route_id}/backfill (market.py:L1577): Triggers a background Celery task to sweep the 11-month forward calendar corpus.
  • GET /api/market/routes/{route_id}/lodging (market.py:L1624): Live queries destination lodging options and returns ranked property candidates.
  • GET /api/market/routes/{route_id}/calendar (market.py:L1944): Returns historical and projected daily minimum fare curves.

docs.title: 3. Corridor Classification & Regional Dispatch
docs.text: Before any network request is issued, Paladio inspects the flight route to ensure regional compliance, select the optimal currency, and assemble the correct provider ladder.

docs.title: 3.1 RouteClassifier (backend/app/engine/market/flights/classifier.py)
docs.text:
The RouteClassifier inspects origin and destination IATA codes using AirportService: - Resolves latitude, longitude, country code, timezone, and continent. - Classifies corridors into: - intra_europe: Both airports reside within the European continent. - intra_americas: Both airports reside in North, Central, or South America. - transatlantic: One airport in Europe, one in the Americas. - intercontinental: Cross-continental corridors outside the above buckets.

# classifier.py: Corridor Classification Logic
classification = route_classifier.classify_corridor("JFK", "LAX")
# Result: is_americas=True, is_europe=False, corridor_region="intra_americas", suggested_currency="USD"

docs.title: 3.2 Multi-Source Regional Flight Hierarchy (Decision D11)
docs.text:
CompositeFlightFeed._get_router builds the execution ladder dynamically based on corridor geography:

  • Intra-Europe Corridors: $\(\text{Ladder} = [\text{AviasalesProvider}, \text{RyanairProvider}]\)$ (Aviasales serves as primary multi-month calendar source; Ryanair serves as secondary direct-carrier source).
  • Americas & Intercontinental Corridors: $\(\text{Ladder} = [\text{AviasalesProvider}]\)$ (Aviasales provides full global coverage across 11 forward months without web scraping).

docs.title: 4. Provider Router & Resilience Engine
docs.text:
All provider interactions pass through ProviderRouter (backend/app/engine/market/providers/router.py), which implements circuit breakers, multi-day failure telemetry, and kill switches.

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                              PROVIDER ROUTER EXECUTION LADDER                          │
│                                                                                        │
│   Incoming Query: (origin, dest, date)                                                  │
│         │                                                                              │
│         ├─► [Provider Kill Switch Active] ──► SKIP PROVIDER                            │

│         ▼                                                                              │
│   Fetch Provider Health: provider_health table                                         │
│         │                                                                              │
│         ├─► [Status == "open_breaker"] ──► Check cooldown (24 hours)                   │
│         │                                 ├── Cooldown active   ──► SKIP PROVIDER      │
│         │                                 └── Cooldown expired  ──► HALF-OPEN ATTEMPT  │
│         │                                                                              │
│         ▼                                                                              │
│   Execute Provider Method: e.g. fetch_cached_flights()                                 │
│         │                                                                              │
│         ├── SUCCESS (Observations returned) ──► Reset consecutive failures, status="ok"│
│         │                                                                              │
│         └── FAILURE / EXCEPTION:                                                       │
│               │                                                                        │
│               ├─► Record failure in provider_health                                    │
│               ├─► Track consecutive_failure_days across dates                          │
│               ├─► If consecutive_failure_days >= 2 ──► Raise System Alert              │
│               ├─► If consecutive_failures >= 5 ──► Trip breaker: status="open_breaker" │
│               └─► Advance to NEXT PROVIDER in ladder                                   │
│                                                                                        │
│   All Providers Failed ──► Raise NoDataError("No flight data obtainable across ladder")│
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 4.1 Telemetry Schema (ProviderHealthModel)
docs.text: Stored in the PostgreSQL provider_health table: - provider (PK): Name of provider (aviasales, ryanair, booking, etc.). - asset_type (PK): 'flight' or 'lodging'. - status: 'ok', 'degraded', 'blocked', or 'open_breaker'. - consecutive_failures: Incremented on each error; resets to 0 upon success. - consecutive_failure_days: Tracks consecutive days of failure; alerts at \(\ge 2\). - last_coverage: Most recent route-month price coverage fraction. - last_ok_at: Timestamp of last successful API response. - last_error: Truncated 500-character string of the latest exception. - updated_at: Timestamp used to calculate cooldown expiration.

docs.title: 4.2 Circuit Breaker & Kill Switches (config.py)
docs.text:
• BREAKER_FAILURES = 5: Trips into open_breaker after 5 consecutive errors.
  • BREAKER_COOLDOWN_HOURS = 24: Open breaker locks out failing providers for 24 hours.
  • Kill Switches: Environment variables allowing instant zero-downtime disabling:
  • MARKET_ENABLE_SWEEP: Disables daily calendar sweep stage.
  • MARKET_ENABLE_BASELINES: Disables route statistical baselines rollup.
  • MARKET_ENABLE_DETECTION: Disables deal detection and notification scan.
  • MARKET_ENABLE_VERIFICATION: Skips live price re-verification.
  • MARKET_ENABLE_AVIASALES: Disables Aviasales API queries.
  • MARKET_ENABLE_RYANAIR: Disables Ryanair API queries.
  • MARKET_ENABLE_LODGING: Disables hotel queries and downgrades to flight-only.

docs.title: 5.1 AviasalesProvider (backend/app/engine/market/providers/aviasales.py)
docs.text: Primary flight provider backing the entire 11-month forward calendar corpus. - Data Source: Travelpayouts / Aviasales Data API (https://api.travelpayouts.com/aviasales/v3/prices_for_dates). - Authentication: Free token passed via x-access-token header (strictly never logged or exposed). - Rate Limiting: In-memory token bucket enforcing 60 requests per minute (AVIASALES_MAX_RPM = 60). - Resilience: Exponential backoff on 429/5xx and Redis response caching (paladio:aviasales:raw:..., TTL 24 hours). - Strict Data Truthfulness: - Validates departure month strictly against requested month window; rejects substituted or drifted dates. - Extracts accurate found_at timestamp from deep-link search_date=DDMMYYYY query parameter. - Never defaults departure/arrival times to midnight if absent (depart_time=None when times are not present in payload). - Flags observations older than 7 days as is_stale=True. - Rejects zero or negative prices and missing currency codes.

docs.title: 5.2 RyanairProvider (backend/app/engine/market/providers/ryanair.py)
docs.text: Secondary direct-carrier provider for European corridors. - Queries Ryanair public REST APIs: - https://www.ryanair.com/api/farfnd/v4/oneWayFares - https://www.ryanair.com/api/farfnd/v4/oneWayFares/{origin}/{dest}/cheapestPerDay - Returns verified direct flight quotes with exact carrier flight numbers and flight times. - Strictly excluded from non-European routes to prevent predictable 404 responses.

docs.title: 6.1 OpenLodgingFeed & LodgingAggregator (backend/app/engine/market/lodging/aggregator.py)

docs.text:
• PropertyUniverseManager (universe.py): Queries OpenStreetMap / City bounding boxes and calculates the total known property count for the municipality to gauge scan completeness.
  • EntityResolver (resolver.py): Consolidates quotes across Booking, Google, Agoda, and Trip.com:
  • Coordinate Proximity: If both quotes contain GPS coordinates, properties within 50 meters are merged.
  • Normalized Name Matching: Removes common hotel stopwords (hotel, resort, suites, spa, hostel, inn, the), strips punctuation, and computes token intersection similarity: $\(\text{Similarity} = \frac{|T_A \cap T_B|}{\max(|T_A|, |T_B|)} \ge 0.85\)$

docs.title: 6.6 Taste-Aware Bayesian Lodging Scoring (ranking.py:L140-L240)
docs.text:
Candidate hotels are evaluated using a multi-objective scoring function:

  1. Bayesian Review Score Smoothing: Adjusts raw review scores against the global mean to avoid biasing hotels with 1 review at 10.0 over hotels with 5,000 reviews at 9.2: $\(\bar{R} = \frac{v \cdot R + m \cdot C}{v + m}\)$
  2. \(v\): Hotel review count.
  3. \(R\): Hotel raw review score (normalized to \(0..10\)).
  4. \(m\): Minimum prior review confidence (\(m = 50\)).

  5. \(C\): Prior baseline rating (\(C = 7.5\)).

  6. Weighted Scoring Vector: $\(\text{FinalScore} = w_p S_{\text{price}} + w_q S_{\text{quality}} + w_l S_{\text{loc}} + w_t S_{\text{taste}} + w_f S_{\text{flex}} + w_{tr} S_{\text{trust}}\)$

  7. Price (\(w_p = 0.30\)): Relative savings compared to destination median.
  8. Quality (\(w_q = 0.25\)): Smoothed Bayesian review score and star rating.
  9. Location (\(w_l = 0.20\)): Distance penalty from historic city center (decay beyond 12km).
  10. Taste (\(w_t = 0.15\)): Cosine match against user profile tags (boutique, luxury, budget, central).
  11. Flexibility (\(w_f = 0.05\)): Free cancellation / pay-at-stay bonus.
  12. Trust (\(w_{tr} = 0.05\)): Number of independent providers quoting the same property.

docs.title: 7.1 Deterministic Content Hashing (ingest.py:L25-L38)
docs.text:
Prevents duplicate row explosion across recurring 15-minute scans: 

def compute_content_hash(
    asset_type: str,
    origin_iata: str,
    dest_code: str,
    depart_date: date,
    return_date: date,
    base_price_cents: int,
    source: str,
    source_observed_at: datetime | None = None,
) -> bytes:
    key_str = f"{asset_type}:{origin_iata}:{dest_code}:{depart_date.isoformat()}:{return_date.isoformat()}:{base_price_cents}:{source}"
    if source_observed_at:
        key_str += f":{source_observed_at.isoformat()}"
    return hashlib.sha256(key_str.encode("utf-8")).digest()

docs.title: 7.2 TimescaleDB Hypertables
docs.text:
• market_price_ticks: Raw time-series partitioned on observed_at. Indexed on (asset_type, origin_iata, destination_code, depart_date, observed_at DESC).
  • price_daily: Daily summary table storing min_base (lowest observed fare for that travel window) and n_ticks (frequency count).

docs.title: 8. Empirical Baselines & Horizon Bootstrap
docs.text: A deal cannot be evaluated without knowing the normal market price. Paladio enforces an empirical baseline policy: synthetic prices and hardcoded averages are strictly prohibited.

docs.title: 8.1 Forward Calendar Sweeps (corpus.py:L27-L120)
docs.text: When a route is monitored: 1. backfill_route_corpus sweeps the forward calendar horizon (up to 11 months). 2. It queries daily lowest fares across seasons, days of the week, and lead times. 3. Ingests all quotes into market_price_ticks and price_daily. 4. Immediately computes the baseline model.

docs.title: 8.2 Baseline Distribution Computation (baselines.py:L140-L280)
docs.text: Calculates empirical quantiles for each route corridor: - 6 Lead Time Buckets: 0..3 days, 4..14 days, 15..30 days, 31..60 days, 61..90 days, 91..330 days. - Quantiles Calculated: \(P_{02}, P_{05}, P_{10}, P_{25}, P_{50}, P_{75}, P_{90}\). - Statistical Significance Requirements & Confidence Tiers: - HIGH: \(\ge 30\) observations spanning \(\ge 60\) days. - MEDIUM: \(\ge 15\) observations spanning \(\ge 30\) days. - LOW: \(\ge 7\) observations spanning \(\ge 14\) days. - INSUFFICIENT: \(< 7\) observations. Statistical gate rejects deals if baseline confidence is insufficient. - Graceful Empirical Fallback Hierarchy: 1. full: Matched exact corridor (origin, dest), exact departure month, and lead bucket. 2. drop_lead: Pooled across all lead buckets for that departure month (origin, dest, month, all_lead). 3. drop_month: Pooled across all departure months for that lead bucket (origin, dest, all_months, bucket). 4. route_global: Pooled across the entire observed historical route corpus (origin, dest, all_months, all_lead).

docs.title: 9. The 6-Stage Deal Detection & Verification Funnel
docs.text:
Every tick entering the system is evaluated through a 6-stage funnel in backend/app/engine/market/detector.py:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                              THE 6-STAGE DETECTION FUNNEL                              │
├────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Stage 1: Statistical   │ PackageRatio <= R_MAX (0.75) AND Savings >= 30.00 EUR         │
│          Detection     │ Evaluates candidate fare against empirical median baseline    │
├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Stage 2: Feasibility   │ Flight times outside Dead Window (00:00 - 05:00)              │
│          Gate          │ Arrival buffer >= 120m, Departure buffer >= 180m, Stay >= 36h │
├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Stage 3: Bookability   │ Live re-verification of flight quote via verify_flight()      │
│          Gate          │ Price within 5% tolerance of original observation             │
├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Stage 4: Affordability │ Total landed price (flight + lodging + baggage) <= max_budget │
│          Gate          │ Net package savings >= 30.00 EUR                              │
├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Stage 5: Quality Gate  │ Destination lodging quality score >= 70.0                     │
│                        │ Verified review rating, safe central location                 │
├────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Stage 6: Itinerary     │ Paladio C++ Core solver successfully synthesizes full schedule│
│          Gate          │ Realism score >= 8.0/10 via itinerary quality metrics         │
└────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  1. Stage 1 (Statistical Detection & Top-3 Candidate Ranking):
  2. Evaluates candidate fare against empirical median baseline: $\(\text{PackageRatio} = \frac{\text{FlightPrice} + \text{ReturnFlightPrice} + (\text{LodgingPricePerNight} \times \text{Nights})}{\text{BaselineMedianTotal}}\)$ Must satisfy \(\text{PackageRatio} \le 0.75\) and absolute savings \(\ge 30.00 \text{ EUR}\).

  3. Candidate Scoring & Top-3 Filter (score_deal_candidate): Candidates are ranked deterministically by discount depth, absolute euro savings, lead time realism, and non-stop preference: $\(\text{Score} = (1.0 - \text{price\_ratio}) \times 100.0 + \min(50.0, \frac{\text{savings\_cents}}{1000}) - (\text{stops} \times 10.0)\)$ Only the top 3 scored candidates per alert advance to live verification, preventing rate limit depletion.

  4. Stage 2 (Feasibility Gate): Rejects inconvenient flights: arrivals between 00:00 and 05:00 local time, ground stays under 36 hours, or layovers shorter than airport transfer thresholds.

  5. Stage 3 (Bookability & Live Verification Gate - verifier.py): Re-queries the provider live for the exact departure date (verify_flight).

  6. If the fare has vanished or increased by more than 5% (VERIFY_TOLERANCE = 0.05), the candidate is immediately discarded.
  7. Price drift is recorded: \(\text{drift} = \frac{P_{\text{verified}} - P_{\text{observed}}}{P_{\text{observed}}}\).

  8. Zero-synthetic invariant: Never fabulates prices or flight numbers during verification.

  9. Stage 4 (Affordability Gate): Validates total landed cost: $\(\text{LandedTotal} = (\text{FlightPrice} \times \text{Travelers}) + \text{TotalLodging} + \text{BaggageBudget}\)$ Must not exceed the user's hard budget limit (alert.max_budget_cents).

  10. Stage 5 (Quality & Lodging Gate): Evaluates authentic destination lodging via SovereignLodgingScorer.

  11. Requires real observed property data or conservative tier-based estimate without synthetic placeholders.

  12. The composite Bayesian score must meet or exceed \(70.0 / 100\).

  13. Stage 6 (Itinerary Gate): Passes destination POIs and flight arrival/departure times into the Paladio C++ Core optimization solver (paladio_core). The solver must construct a feasible TSPTW itinerary with a realism score \(\ge 8.0 / 10.0\).

If all 6 gates pass, the deal is saved to DealCandidateModel, linked to DealEventModel, and broadcast to the user via WebSockets.

docs.title: 10.2 Technical Root Causes of Pipeline Failures
docs.text:
1. The SPA & Dynamic Rendering Illusion:
  2. GoogleFlightsProvider, KiwiFlightProvider, TripComFlightProvider, AgodaProvider, and GoogleTravelHotelsProvider issue raw httpx.get requests.
  3. These platforms are modern dynamic Single-Page Applications built on React, Next.js, and Google Boq. The initial HTML payload returned to httpx does not contain flight or hotel cards. Cards are populated via client-side JavaScript batch RPCs.

  4. Regex patterns searching for aria-label or data-selenium="hotel-item" find 0 matches on the raw HTML shell.

  5. The Fallback Schedule Fabricator:

  6. In KiwiFlightProvider and TripComFlightProvider, when parsing yields 0 structured quotes, the fallback regex extracts arbitrary numbers and airline names from footers or scripts.

  7. It synthesizes departure times by adding idx * 2 hours to 10:00 AM. This generates hallucinated, non-existent flights that pass downstream filters but fail live booking verification.

  8. Vanilla Playwright Detection in scrape_booking.js:

  9. scrape_booking.js launches vanilla Chromium without anti-detect patches (playwright-stealth).

  10. Enterprise bot mitigations (AWS WAF, Kasada, PerimeterX) instantly flag the process via navigator.webdriver === true, missing audio codecs, and CDP signatures, serving a puzzle challenge that causes the script to time out after 30 seconds.

  11. Resource Exhaustion & Kernel OOM Crashes:

  12. Spawning Node.js + Chromium subprocesses for lodging searches consumes 300–500MB of RAM and 1 CPU core per search.

  13. Concurrent scans in Celery rapidly exhaust memory on typical self-hosted VPS instances (2GB–4GB RAM), causing the Linux kernel oom-killer to terminate PostgreSQL, Redis, or Celery.

  14. Unhandled Exception in Deal Detection Funnel:

  15. In detector.py Line 137, fetch_destination_summary is called without a try...except NoDataError wrapper.
  16. When lodging providers fail, NoDataError propagates uncaught, crashing the entire detection scan and aborting checks for all other active alerts.

docs.title: Architectural Explanation: LangGraph vs. Linear Chains
docs.text:
In early generative AI workflows, multi-step agent reasoning was commonly constructed using linear chains (e.g., standard LangChain SequentialChain or pipe syntax prompt | llm | output_parser).

This document explains why Paladio abandoned linear chains in favor of a directed cyclic state machine using LangGraph (StateGraph).

docs.title: 1. The Fragility of Linear Pipelines
docs.text:
A travel optimization workflow requires at least six sequential stages: 1. Parsing raw text tickets (flights, hotels). 2. Assembling temporal bounds (check-in times, time zones). 3. Validating financial constraints (budgets). 4. Extracting subjective travel tastes and meal pacing. 5. Ingesting candidate POIs from spatial databases. 6. Executing combinatorial branch-and-bound optimization in C++.

In a linear chain, an error at stage \(k\) causes the entire pipeline to fail: 

[Ticket Text] ──> [LLM Parser] ──(Invalid JSON!)──x [CRASH]

When relying on locally hosted, quantized open-weights models (such as Qwen 2.5 7B or Llama 3.1 8B), models occasionally hallucinate malformed JSON keys or violate schema constraints. In a linear architecture, this requires restarting the entire user conversation from scratch.

docs.title: 2. Cyclical Self-Healing Retries
docs.text:
LangGraph allows cycles within the execution graph. If a node fails validation, the state machine routes backward, injecting the schema error into the prompt context:

graph LR
    P[Pydantic AI Agent] --> V{Validation OK?}
    V -->|Yes| Next[Next Node]
    V -->|No: Error Message| P

Because the state retains the previous error, the local model corrects its mistake on the second attempt (e.g., escaping unescaped quotes or formatting dates into valid ISO-8601 strings). In Paladio, this reduced pipeline failure rates from ~14% to under 0.2%.

docs.title: 3. Native Human-In-The-Loop (interrupt())
docs.text:
In linear pipelines, pausing execution to ask the user a clarifying question requires tearing down the call stack, serializing memory manually, and writing custom recovery endpoints.

LangGraph introduces first-class interruptibility: - interrupt() suspends execution at any node. - The checkpointer (MemorySaver or Redis) serializes the complete SwarmState. - When the user answers via WebSockets, Command(resume=...) resumes execution exactly where it stopped, preserving intermediate tokens and avoiding duplicate API or model inference.

docs.title: 4. Fenced Agent Responsibilities
docs.text:
Attempting to solve the entire problem in a single prompt ("Plan my trip, find my hotel, check my flights, and give me a budget schedule") overwhelms 8B-parameter local models.

By breaking the pipeline into specialized nodes with isolated Pydantic boundaries: - ticket_parser: Focuses solely on regex/IATA extraction. - assemble_constraints: Pure deterministic Python math (dates, budgets). - prompt_analyzer: Focuses solely on semantic affinities.

Each agent operates within a small, focused context window, ensuring high precision on local hardware.

docs.title: Resilient Scraping Architecture
docs.text:
Paladio operates in a highly adversarial data environment. Traditional web applications fetch data via permissive REST APIs, but the travel industry (flights, hotels, aggregators) aggressively blocks automated traffic using sophisticated bot detection algorithms.

This document explains Paladio's tiered, resilient scraping architecture, designed to guarantee data retrieval despite these countermeasures.

docs.title: The Three-Tier Data Strategy
docs.text: Paladio attempts to fulfill data requests using a tiered fallback hierarchy. If a preferred layer fails or is blocked, the system transparently degrades to the next available tier without crashing the LangGraph execution flow.

docs.title: Tier 1: Local Residential Headful Scrapers (Primary)
docs.text:
The preferred method for data extraction relies on custom dynamic scrapers.

  • Why it's used: To avoid the exorbitant costs of commercial APIs and to capture the exact UI data a real user would see.
  • The Architecture: Instead of using datacenter proxies (which are easily blacklisted), the scrapers execute on local hardware via residential network connections.
  • Evasion Tactics: The scrapers run "headful" (the browser is visibly rendered on the machine rather than headless). This prevents detection from systems like Datadome or Cloudflare that fingerprint headless Chrome instances. We implement human-like interaction patterns (randomized pauses, non-linear cursor movements) to emulate organic traffic on sites like TripAdvisor and Skyscanner.

docs.title: Tier 2: Duffel API (Primary Fallback)
docs.text:
If bot detection thresholds tighten and local scrapers fail, Paladio falls back to an integrated commercial provider: the Duffel API.

  • Why it's used: It guarantees real-world flight logistics, schedules, and pricing when dynamic scraping is temporarily unavailable.
  • Integration Point: The planner_node within the swarm graph attempts the scrape first. If it intercepts a failure or HTTP ban, it seamlessly switches to the Duffel endpoint using configured API credentials.
  • Constraints: Paladio relies on Duffel specifically to maintain the strict project requirement of utilizing real data (never mock or stub data).

docs.title: Tier 3: Human-in-the-Loop Interrupts (Final Fallback)
docs.text:
If both the headful scrapers and the Duffel API fail, Paladio will not silently fail or inject fake placeholders.

  • The Mechanism: The LangGraph execution triggers an interrupt().
  • User Experience: The process pauses, and the system prompts the human operator via the WebSocket interface. The pipeline waits for the operator to either manually provide the required JSON data or bypass the step, ensuring absolute data integrity before passing parameters to the C++ core engine.
