docs.title: 1. Overview & Goals
docs.text: This document outlines the architectural design for a client-side notification system in Paladio's Next.js frontend. The system provides: - User-Isolated Storage: Notifications are partitioned per authenticated user (user.id) in localStorage. - Hybrid Triggering: Automatic capture of engine/WebSocket telemetry events (solver completion, errors, clarification requests) alongside a simple imperative notify API for React components and user actions. - Rich Timestamps: Every notification includes an ISO timestamp formatted into readable date & time plus relative time indicators. - Interactive UI Surfaces: A notification bell with unread badge in the sidebar/navigation, a slide-out/dropdown notification center with read/clear controls and actionable links, and transient floating toasts for real-time alerts.

docs.title: 2.1 Type Definitions (frontend/src/types/notification.ts)
docs.text:
export type NotificationType = 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error';

export interface NotificationItem {
  id: string;
  userId: string;
  type: NotificationType;
  title: string;
  message: string;
  timestamp: string; // ISO 8601 (e.g., "2026-09-16T17:40:00.000Z")
  read: boolean;
  actionLink?: string; // e.g., "/engine", "/vault"
  actionLabel?: string; // e.g., "View Itinerary"
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export interface ToastItem {
  id: string;
  notification: NotificationItem;
  durationMs: number;
}

docs.title: 2.2 Storage Isolation Strategy
docs.text:
• Key Schema: paladio_notifications_${userId}. If no user is logged in, fallback to paladio_notifications_guest.
  • User Switching: When user in AuthContext changes:
  • The active storage key is updated.
  • The store rehydrates with the new user's notification list.
  • No cross-user data leakage is possible.
  • Quota & Retention Policy:
  • Maximum 100 notifications per user.
  • Automatically drops the oldest notifications when limit is reached (FIFO).
  • Storage operations are wrapped in try/catch to handle private browsing or quota limits gracefully.

docs.title: 3.1 Store: useNotificationStore (frontend/src/stores/notificationStore.ts)
docs.text:
Built using Zustand (^5.0.15):

interface NotificationState {
  currentUserId: string | null;
  notifications: NotificationItem[];
  toasts: ToastItem[];
  unreadCount: number;

  // Actions
  initUser: (userId: string | null) => void;
  addNotification: (params: Omit<NotificationItem, 'id' | 'timestamp' | 'read' | 'userId'>) => NotificationItem;
  markAsRead: (id: string) => void;
  markAllAsRead: () => void;
  removeNotification: (id: string) => void;
  clearAll: () => void;
  dismissToast: (toastId: string) => void;
}

docs.title: 3.2 Imperative Dispatcher API (frontend/src/utils/notify.ts)
docs.text:
A clean helper for components: 

export const notify = {
  info: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
  success: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
  warning: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
  error: (title: string, message: string, options?: Partial<NotificationItem>) => ...,
};

docs.title: 4.1 Bridge Hook: useSocketNotificationBridge (frontend/src/hooks/useSocketNotificationBridge.ts)
docs.text:
Subscribes to telemetry from SocketContext or wraps the socket handler to generate relevant alerts: - EVALUATING_ROUTES (status completed / recovered): Emits success notification: "Itinerary Generated — Route and transit plan is ready." with action link to /engine or /vault. - CLARIFICATION_NEEDED: Emits warning notification: "Input Required — Solver requires additional constraints." with action link to /engine. - ERROR: Emits error notification: "Engine Fault — Inference failed." - FEEDBACK_PROCESSED: Emits info notification: "Preference Model Updated".

Duplicate suppression is built-in so re-renders or socket reconnects do not trigger duplicate notifications.

docs.title: Design Specification: Paladio Core Open-Source Showcase & Architecture Documentation
docs.text:
• Date: 2026-09-23
  • Author: Paladio Core Systems & Operations Research Team
  • Target Repository: Leandro-Juan/paladio-core (synchronized from cpp_core/ via GitHub Actions)
  • Primary Goal: Transform paladio-core into an elite, production-grade, star-worthy public repository with comprehensive Diátaxis documentation, empirical benchmarks, Apache 2.0 license, and modern C++/Python packaging.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Value Proposition
docs.text:
paladio-core is an ultra-fast, deterministic C++20 engine with zero-copy Python (pybind11) bindings designed to solve the Time-Constrained Orienteering Problem with Time Windows (TCOPTW), budget constraints, and real-world human travel constraints.

Combinatorial routing with budget and time windows is strongly NP-hard. Exploring all permutations on an \(N\)-node graph requires \(O(N!)\) operations, making naive depth-first search infeasible for \(N > 10\). paladio-core achieves microsecond-to-millisecond execution times by combining: 1. Continuous Fractional Knapsack Upper Bounding: An admissible linear relaxation that computes an upper bound on remaining score in \(O(N)\) at each search node, pruning subtrees that cannot surpass the incumbent solution. 2. Compact 64-Bit Bitmask State Encoding: Node visitation, mandatory milestones, and category sets are stored as bit patterns in uint64_t registers, enabling \(O(1)\) operations with hardware intrinsics (std::countr_zero). 3. Dominance Pruning & State Memoization: Multi-criteria Pareto-dominance pruning that eliminates paths that arrive later, at higher cost, or with lower score than previously explored trajectories for equivalent visited subsets. 4. Zero-Allocation Hot-Path Architecture: Zero dynamic memory allocations (malloc/new) inside the core branch-and-bound recursion, ensuring maximum cache locality and deterministic low latency.

High-Performance Architecture Highlights: - \(O(1)\) State Transitions: Node visitation bitmasks and category histories are tracked in 64-bit unsigned integers (uint64_t), utilizing compiler and CPU intrinsics (std::countr_zero). - Zero Heap Allocation in Hot Loops: DFS call frames, path tracking (std::array<int, 64>), and category counts (std::array<uint8_t, 8>) reside on contiguous stack memory without calling malloc or new during branch exploration. - Sanitizer Clean: 100% verified under Clang/GCC AddressSanitizer (ASan), LeakSanitizer (LSan), and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (UBSan). - GIL-Free Concurrency: Python bindings release the Global Interpreter Lock (pybind11::gil_scoped_release), allowing pure multi-threaded C++ scaling across CPU cores.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Value Proposition
docs.text:
Paladio is an air-gapped, 100% sovereign travel intelligence and combinatorial optimization platform designed for self-hosted execution via Docker. It solves a core architectural challenge in applied AI systems: bridging stochastic, conversational multi-agent workflows with differentiable real-time machine learning, deterministic sub-millisecond mathematical combinatorial optimization, and rich interactive geospatial visualizations.

This project serves as Leandro Juan's flagship CV demonstration of distributed backend engineering, state-machine agent orchestration, applied machine learning, database indexing, and clean systems architecture.

docs.title: Core Architectural Pillars
docs.text:
1. LangGraph Multi-Agent Swarm: StateGraph orchestration with cyclical self-healing retries, Pydantic AI validation guardrails, and non-blocking human-in-the-loop interruption via interrupt().
  2. Sovereign Machine Learning & Continuous Learning: 768-D semantic RAG using local embeddings (nomic-embed-text via Ollama) and pgvector, continuous online Exponential Moving Average (EMA) user taste learning, continuous-to-discrete harmonic projection to 8-D radar telemetry, and Bayesian multi-attribute utility scoring (HybridSovereignScorer).

docs.title: Design Specification: Global TSPTW with Soft Time-Window Constraints
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-16 Status: Approved Author: Antigravity

docs.title: 1. Context & Motivation
docs.text:
Previously, re-optimizing an itinerary day partitioned the sequence into isolated sub-tours bounded by fixed anchors (hotels, airports, or user-locked POIs). While this prevented locked items from moving, it fragmented the global optimization problem into piecewise sub-problems. If a user locked a stop at mid-day, the solver could not optimize across the boundary, causing artificial zig-zagging and sub-optimal overall routes.

This specification designs a unified global Traveling Salesperson Problem with Time Windows (TSPTW) solver in C++20 (paladio_core), replacing piecewise array partitioning with soft time-window constraints \([t_{\text{target}} - \epsilon, t_{\text{target}} + \epsilon]\).

docs.title: 2.1 Graph & Node Attributes
docs.text: Let \(G = (V, E)\) be a complete directed graph with \(n = |V|\) POIs, and transit duration matrix \(T \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^{n \times n}\). Each vertex \(i \in V\) is associated with: - \(D_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\): Dwell duration (minutes). - \([W_i^{\min}, W_i^{\max}]\): Permissible arrival window (minutes from midnight). - For locked POIs at scheduled arrival time \(t_{\text{target}}\): $\(W_i^{\min} = \max(t_{\text{day\_start}}, t_{\text{target}} - \epsilon), \quad W_i^{\max} = \min(t_{\text{day\_end}}, t_{\text{target}} + \epsilon)\)$ Default \(\epsilon = 15\) minutes (30-minute arrival window). - For unlocked POIs: $\(W_i^{\min} = \max(t_{\text{day\_start}}, \text{earliest\_time}_i), \quad W_i^{\max} = \min(t_{\text{day\_end}}, \text{latest\_time}_i)\)$ - For the start depot (node 0, e.g. morning hotel): $\(W_0^{\min} = W_0^{\max} = t_{\text{day\_start}}\)$ - For a fixed end depot (node \(n-1\), e.g. night hotel return): Fixed at permutation index \(n-1\).

docs.title: 2.2 Forward Timeline Simulation
docs.text: For any tour permutation \(\pi = (\pi_0, \pi_1, \dots, \pi_{n-1})\): 1. Initialize arrival and departure at start depot: $\(t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_0) = W_{\pi_0}^{\min}, \quad t_{\text{dep}}(\pi_0) = t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_0) + D_{\pi_0}\)$ 2. For \(k = 1, \dots, n-1\): $\(t_{\text{transit}} = T[\pi_{k-1}, \pi_k]\)$ $\(t_{\text{reach}} = t_{\text{dep}}(\pi_{k-1}) + t_{\text{transit}}\)$ $\(t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_k) = \max(t_{\text{reach}}, W_{\pi_k}^{\min})\)$ $\(t_{\text{dep}}(\pi_k) = t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_k) + D_{\pi_k}\)$

docs.title: 2.3 Soft Penalty Objective
docs.text: $\(\text{Cost}(\pi) = \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} T[\pi_{k-1}, \pi_k] + \lambda_{\text{penalty}} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \left( \max(0, t_{\text{reach}}(\pi_k) - W_{\pi_k}^{\max}) \right)^2\)$ Where: - \(\lambda_{\text{penalty}} = 100.0\): Heavily penalizes arriving after \(W^{\max}\), driving the solver to meet locked windows without discarding candidates. - Idling before \(W^{\min}\) is accounted for in \(t_{\text{arr}}(\pi_k) = \max(t_{\text{reach}}, W_{\pi_k}^{\min})\) without extra penalty, representing natural waiting time.

docs.title: 3.1 Function Signature (cpp_core/include/paladio/engine.hpp)
docs.text:
[[nodiscard]] std::vector<int> solve_tsptw(
    const int *transit_durations, int n,
    const int *dwell_times,
    const int *window_starts,
    const int *window_ends,
    int start_node = 0,
    int end_node = -1,
    bool fixed_end = false,
    double penalty_weight = 100.0);

docs.title: 3.2 Optimization Engine (cpp_core/src/engine.cpp)
docs.text:
1. Initial Solution Generation:
  2. Multi-start greedy heuristic combining nearest neighbor with earliest deadline sorting (\(W_i^{\min}\)).
  3. Generates up to 8 diverse valid starting permutations.
  4. Local Search Improvements:
  5. 2-Opt Edge Inversion: Iteratively reverses tour sub-sequences \([\pi_i, \dots, \pi_j]\) whenever the total cost (transit + window penalty) decreases.
  6. Or-Opt Node Relocation: Relocates single nodes and consecutive pairs to candidate insertion slots that minimize cost.
  7. Performance & Determinism Guarantees:
  8. Zero heap allocation in hot loop (pre-allocated working arrays).
  9. Worst-case execution time under 10ms for \(n \le 25\).
  10. Releases Python GIL via pybind11::gil_scoped_release.

docs.title: 4.1 Pybind11 Binding (cpp_core/src/bindings.cpp)
docs.text: Expose solve_tsptw taking flattened 1D numpy arrays for durations, dwell_times, window_starts, window_ends, integers n, start_node, end_node, boolean fixed_end, and float penalty_weight.

docs.title: 4.2 Reoptimization Service (backend/app/services/trip_reoptimization_service.py)
docs.text:
1. In reoptimize_trip_slice:
  2. Inspect items of the target day.
  3. For each item, compute dwell duration and time windows \([W^{\min}, W^{\max}]\) based on locked status.
  4. If locked: center tight window around current scheduled start (\(t \pm \epsilon\)).
  5. If unlocked: set window to operating hours or \([t_{\text{day\_start}}, t_{\text{day\_end}}]\).
  6. Call paladio_core.solve_tsptw(...) over the entire day's nodes in one single call.
  7. Reconstruct the day's timeline with arrival/departure times.

docs.title: Design Specification: Bi-directional Route Monitoring & Round-Trip Calendar Matrix
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-21 Status: Approved Author: Antigravity

docs.title: 1. Context & Motivation
docs.text:
Currently, Paladio's route monitoring pipeline only tracks unidirectional outbound flights (origin_iata -> destination_code). When a user monitors a corridor like Madrid (MAD) to Berlin (BER), only outbound flight ticks are ingested, stored, and plotted in the Price Trend Graph and Multi-Month Price Matrix. Furthermore, the proactive deal detection engine calculates package savings by combining outbound ticks with estimated lodging, omitting actual return flight pricing.

This specification designs: 1. Bi-directional Corpus Ingestion: Ingesting and maintaining price baselines for both outbound (A -> B) and return (B -> A) flights. 2. Dual-Trend Price Graph: Simultaneous rendering of Outbound and Return forward curves / historical prices, with a quick segment toggle ([ BOTH ] [ OUTBOUND ] [ RETURN ]). 3. Multi-Month Round-Trip Calendar Matrix: - Direction toggles: [ OUTBOUND ] [ RETURN ] [ BEST ROUND-TRIP ]. - Pricing sub-toggle for Round-Trip mode: [ FLIGHTS ONLY ] [ FLIGHT + HOTEL ]. - Horizon toggle limited strictly to [ 4M ] and [ FULL HORIZON ] (up to 11 months). - Departure-indexed cells with automatic cheapest return pairing across [min_nights, max_nights]. - Hover and selection range bar highlighting stay duration on the calendar grid. - Drawer with complete flight pairing details, lodging breakdown, direct booking links, and a direct "Plan Itinerary" action. 4. Deal Detection Engine Enhancement: Requiring confirmed, lowest-cost return flights in deal candidate packages.

docs.title: 3.1 Dual-Corpus Ingestion & Celery Tasks
docs.text:
In backend/app/engine/market/corpus.py: - backfill_route_corpus is updated to accept an optional bidirectional: bool = True parameter (default True). - When backfilling route (origin_iata, destination_code), it automatically backfills both: 1. origin_iata -> destination_code 2. destination_code -> origin_iata - RouteCorpusStatusModel maintains health and departure date counts for each directed pair.

In backend/app/engine/market/detector.py: - run_deal_detection_scan() pairs each outbound flight tick ft with matching return flight ticks rt from destination_code -> origin_iata where rt.depart_date == ft.depart_date + timedelta(days=nights). - If no return flight exists for that date, candidate is disqualified or penalized, ensuring verified round trips.

docs.text: Date: 2026-10-21 Author: Antigravity Status: Draft for User Review Canonical Spec Path: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-poi-detail-inspector-photos-design.md

docs.title: 1. Overview & Motivation
docs.text:
When planning trips in Paladio, users searching for or clicking on places (such as Museo del Prado, Royal Palace of Madrid, or any search result/waypoint) currently see only minimal metadata (name, cost, duration, and similarity score) in a small floating card or map popup.

This feature introduces a comprehensive POI Detail Inspector Drawer that slides in from the right edge of the workspace whenever a user clicks a POI anywhere in the interface (Search Engine results, Map pins, or Timeline stops). The inspector displays rich, authoritative operational details and real, high-resolution photography resolved dynamically via Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons, backed by Redis caching.

In accordance with Paladio's core engineering invariants: - Zero Mock Data: All data (photos, descriptions, operating hours, prices) is completely dynamic—loaded from PostgreSQL, OpenStreetMap tags, live Wikimedia/Wikipedia APIs, or runtime calculations. Mock placeholders and synthetic stock photos are strictly forbidden. - Air-Gappable & Self-Hosted: No cloud LLM APIs. Wikimedia photo resolution uses standard public REST/Action APIs and results are cached in Redis (with fallback to local schematic category illustrations if no photo exists for rare nodes).

docs.title: 2. Architecture & Data Flow
docs.text:
[ Frontend: Next.js 16 / React 19 ]
  │
  ├── 1. Click POI (Search Card / Map Marker / Timeline Stop)
  │
  ▼
[ GET /api/v1/pois/{poi_id}/details ]
  │
  ├── 2. Query PostgreSQL `attractions` table by ID
  │      (Pulls hours_known, daily_windows, cost_eur, description, wikidata_id, etc.)
  │

docs.title: 3.3 Service: WikimediaPhotoResolver (backend/app/services/wikimedia_photo_resolver.py)
docs.text:

docs.title: Design Specification: Dedicated Transit Tab Refactor
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Author: Antigravity Status: Draft for User Review & Confirmation Canonical Spec Path: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-transit-tab-design.md Tracking Source: PLAN.md

docs.title: 1. Overview & Motivation
docs.text: Transit stops are currently indexed as generic POIs in the attractions table (with IDs like OSM-transit-<category>-<id>). As a result, they appear indiscriminately in the Search tab alongside museums, restaurants, and sights, showing irrelevant fields on cards and detail inspectors (e.g. "Suggested stay: 10 mins", "% AFFINITY", star ratings, duration/price filters, photo carousels, and opening hours). Furthermore, station cards display a synthetic flat fare (e.g., €1.80 or €2 / person) derived from a citywide fallback, and stop codes (like JB13) are rendered as route badges.

docs.title: Core Objective
docs.text: Move transit out of the Search tab into its own dedicated tab in the Plan left panel (Route, Search, Transit, Saved). Base the new tab on pruned GTFS feeds already compiled for Valhalla, using derived, compact PostgreSQL tables. Preserve existing Valhalla Route legs and itinerary generation completely intact.

docs.title: Key Invariants
docs.text:
• Zero Mock Data & No Fabricated Fallbacks: Values missing in feeds are hidden, explained honestly, or degraded gracefully (e.g. stop-sequence polylines when shapes are absent). No synthetic station prices or color hashing.
  • Air-Gappable & Self-Hosted: 100% local operation without external cloud APIs.
  • Deterministic & High Performance: Derived tables precalculate stop sequences, service spans, headways, and offsets once per feed build. Zero runtime scanning of multi-gigabyte stop_times.txt.
  • Capability-Driven UI: Feeds vary by city (e.g. Tokyo has translations and fares but no shapes; Paris has shapes and transfers but no translations). The UI is a pure function of feed capability flags.

docs.title: 2. Phase 0 Audit Summary

Top-level workspace tabs are Plan, Wallet, Costs, Collab, Photos. Category chips live in PROJECT_CATEGORIES (with 'transit'). Right-hand detail panel is PoiDetailView in TripWorkspace.tsx. No shapes.txt. Dates: 20260314–20270312. docs.title: 3. Architecture & Data Flow
docs.text:
[ Pruned GTFS Feed on Disk (/gtfs_feeds/<city>) ]
                    │
                    ▼ (Triggered after build_city_gtfs_task or backfill CLI)
[ Celery Task: derive_city_transit_task ]
                    │
                    ├── 1. Compute Capability Flags & Date Spans
                    ├── 2. Collapse Platforms -> transit_stations (WGS84 lat/lon indexed)
                    ├── 3. Parse Routes & Normalize Colors -> transit_lines
                    ├── 4. Group Stop Sequences -> transit_patterns & transit_pattern_stops
                    ├── 5. Extract First Departures & Offsets -> transit_pattern_trips
                    ├── 6. Summarize Spans & Headways -> transit_service_summary
                    ├── 7. Optional Shapes / Transfers -> transit_shapes, transit_transfers
                    │
                    ▼ (Single-transaction atomic swap of active_build_id)
[ PostgreSQL: Compact Derived Transit Schema ]
                    │
                    ▼
[ FastAPI: /api/v1/trips/{trip_id}/transit/* & /api/v1/transit/* ]
   ├── /availability     -> City state, capability flags, feed validity
   ├── /nearby           -> Stations grouped by anchor (Lodging + Day stops)
   ├── /lines            -> Lines grouped by agency & mode
   ├── /lines/{id}       -> Pattern geometry, ordered stops
   ├── /stations/{id}    -> Lines, headways, next departures for selected Day

                    │
                    ▼
[ Next.js 16 Frontend: TripUnifiedSidebar (Transit Tab) ]
   ├── State Switcher: Empty / Building / Unavailable / Expired / Ready

docs.title: Design Specification: Interactive Point-to-Point Directions in Transit Tab
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-29 Author: Antigravity Status: Ready for User Review & Evaluation Canonical Spec Path: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-29-transit-point-to-point-directions-design.md Related: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-transit-tab-design.md, PLAN.md

docs.title: 1. Overview & Motivation
docs.text: In the Paladio Trip Workspace, the Transit Tab currently provides two subviews: Nearby (stations within walking distance of trip anchors) and Lines (browsing transit lines and scheduled station departures). However, travelers frequently need to plan ad-hoc journeys between two specific locations in the destination city—such as routing from their hotel to a dinner reservation, between two attractions, or to an arbitrary street address or map location.

docs.title: Core Objective
docs.text: Add an interactive Directions subview to the Transit Tab that enables users to select an Origin and Destination (via dynamic name search, direct coordinate input, or direct click-to-pick on the main workspace map), configure schedule departure/arrival constraints, and compute the most optimal route via public transit or direct walking, adhering to realistic travel heuristics.

docs.title: Key Invariants
docs.text:
• Dynamic Data Only (Zero Hardcoded Mappings): All routing, places, stations, and fare structures are dynamically loaded from PostgreSQL/pgvector, local Valhalla multimodal routing engine, and OpenStreetMap/Photon geocoding.
  • Air-Gappable & Self-Hosted: 100% self-hosted via Docker Compose. No external proprietary cloud LLM or mapping APIs.
  • Icon Integrity (Zero Emojis): Strictly use Paladio bespoke SVG icons (components/icons.tsx), honoring the Japanese Tactical Minimalist / Pacific Jazz design system.
  • Reasonable Route Realism: Never propose walking 1.5 hours when public transit is available, nor taking public transit for a trivial 5-minute walk. The engine automatically classifies and prioritizes the most realistic, sensible primary route.

docs.title: 2.1 Subview Navigation Order
docs.text:
The Transit Tab subview bar is reorganized in priority order: 

[ Directions | Lines | Nearby ]
Directions is the default active subview upon entering the Transit Tab.

docs.title: 2.2 Site Selection (Origin & Destination)
docs.text: Each site input provides three input modalities: 1. Dynamic Name Search with Autocomplete Dropdown: - Zero-query state: clicking the input displays instant quick-pick chips for current trip anchors: - Hotel / Stay Anchor (with address & coordinates) - Airport / Arrival Station - Day POIs (POIs scheduled on the currently selected day) - Saved Bookmarks - Typing queries /api/locations/places?city={destination}&q={query} returning a ranked list with category badges (Attraction, Hotel, Transit Station, Address). 2. Direct Coordinate Input: - Directly typing or pasting latitude/longitude (e.g. 40.4168, -3.7038 or 40.4168 -3.7038) is detected via regex (/^-?\d+(\.\d+)?,\s*-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/), automatically binding coordinates and reverse-geocoding a human-readable display label without hitting search. 3. Direct Click-to-Pick on Workspace Map: - Each input includes a dedicated "Pick on Map" crosshair icon button. - Activating it enters interactive map-pick mode: cursor changes to a crosshair, a tactical banner appears ("Click anywhere on the map to set Origin / Destination"), and clicking any map location or existing marker captures [lat, lng], drops a marker pin, reverse-geocodes the address, and fills the field. 4. Origin <-> Destination Swap: - An icon button between the two fields quickly inverts Origin and Destination coordinates and names.

docs.title: 2.3 Schedule & Departure Controls
docs.text:
• Mode Toggle: [ Depart at | Arrive by ]
  • Calendar Date:
  • Auto-anchored to the active trip day date (getTripDayDate(tripStartDate, dayIndex)).
  • If "All Days" is selected, falls back to the trip start date.
  • Dropdown allows selecting any specific trip day or custom date.
  • Exact Time Picker:
  • Direct time input / selector (HH:MM) defaulting to 09:00 for morning schedules or current city time.

docs.title: 2.4 The Reasonable Route Realism Heuristic
docs.text: When evaluating routes between Origin and Destination: - Both Valhalla Multimodal Transit and Pedestrian routes are computed. - The system determines the primary recommended route: - Walk-Dominant Scenario: If walking time is <= 15 mins (or distance <= 1.2 km) and public transit is slower or comparable (due to walking to station, waiting for headways, or transfers), Direct Walking is presented as the primary route, with Public Transit presented as an alternative option. - Transit-Dominant Scenario: If walking time is > 20 mins (e.g. 45 min, 1.5 hours) and a viable public transit route exists, Public Transit is presented as the primary route, with Walking presented as an alternative reference. - Presentation: - Primary route is rendered in full detail using Paladio's TransitLegView (step maneuvers, colored line badges, stop counts, walking segments, transfer stations, and fare). - Alternative route is presented as a clean toggle card below (e.g., "Compare with Direct Walk: 18 min • 0€" or "Compare with Public Transit: 12 min • €1.50"). Clicking it toggles active inspection and swaps the map polyline.

docs.title: 3. Map Visualization & Synchronization
docs.text:
• Marker Pins:
  • Tactical Pin A for Origin (Slate / Teal palette).
  • Tactical Pin B for Destination (Emerald / Terracotta palette).
  • Route Polylines:
  • Transit segments render in the official line hex color (with a subtle glow layer).
  • Walking segments render as dashed slate polylines with dot markers at turn points.
  • Auto-fit Camera: Map smoothly fits the bounding box of Origin, Destination, and route maneuvers.

docs.title: 4.1 Direction Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /api/trips/{trip_id}/transit/directions (or POST /api/transit/directions)

Request Payload:

  "city": "Madrid",
  "origin": {
    "name": "The Westin Palace",
    "lat": 40.4150,
    "lon": -3.6953
  },
  "destination": {
    "name": "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium",
    "lat": 40.4531,

}
Note: date_time_type: 1 = Depart at, 2 = Arrive by.

Response Payload:

  },

    "mode": "pedestrian",
    "duration_mins": 58,

  },
  "recommendation_reason": "Public transit saves 36 minutes compared to walking (58 mins)."
}

docs.title: 4.2 Unified Places Search Endpoint
docs.text:
GET /api/locations/places?city={city}&q={query}&limit=10

Dynamically resolves: 1. Destination city attractions and hotels from PostgreSQL attractions table. 2. Compiled GTFS transit stations from transit_stations table. 3. OpenStreetMap Photon / Nominatim geocoding spatially biased to the city's bounding box.

docs.title: 5. Testing & Verification Plan
docs.text:
1. Unit Tests (Backend):

docs.title: Specification: .trip File Format & Packaging Engine
docs.text: Date: 2026-11-04 Status: Approved Author: Antigravity & User Target Subsystem: backend/app/trip_package/ and backend/app/api/trips.py

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This document specifies the open, self-contained .trip file standard (application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip) and its backend generation engine for Paladio. A .trip file completely encapsulates a trip: metadata, full itinerary with turn-by-turn route polylines and POIs, wallet tickets with digital barcodes and original binary passes (PDFs/PKPass), group travel expenses and debt settlement matrices, custom collections and packing checklists, and local photos.

The format is engineered to be 100% air-gappable, portable across self-hosted instances, inspectable by standard ZIP utilities, and privacy-conscious with dual export profiles (full_vault and community_shareable).

docs.title: 2.1 Container Structure
docs.text:
The .trip file is an uncompressed or standard deflate ZIP archive. The internal hierarchy is modular:

<trip-name>.trip
├── mimetype                               # ASCII: "application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip"
├── paladio.json                           # Format version, manifest, bounding box, SHA-256 hashes
├── itinerary.json                         # Days, slots, activities, POIs, maneuvers, polylines
├── wallet.json                            # Tickets, booking anchors, barcode payloads, seat/gate info
├── expenses.json                          # Participants, expenses, category splits, settlement matrix
├── collections.json                       # Saved bookmarks, packing lists, custom trip notes
└── attachments/
    ├── tickets/                           # Binary boarding pass PDFs, Apple PKPass files
    └── photos/                            # Trip photos (JPEG/WebP/PNG)

docs.title: 2.2 mimetype File
docs.text:
The first file in the archive must be named mimetype, stored uncompressed (ZIP_STORED), containing: 

application/vnd.paladio.trip+zip

docs.title: 2.3 paladio.json (Root Manifest)
docs.text:
Defines metadata, export parameters, destination context, and cryptographic hashes of all container members: 

{
  "$schema": "https://paladio.app/schemas/v1/trip-package.json",
  "format_version": "1.0.0",
  "generator": {
    "name": "Paladio Backend",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "trip_id": "8f8b0e51-4091-4e4b-97e3-057bf9e34457",
  "export_profile": "full_vault",
  "created_at": "2026-11-04T17:20:00Z",
  "title": "Budapest Thermal & Architectural Tour",
  "destination": "Budapest, Hungary",
  "destination_timezone": "Europe/Budapest",
  "start_date": "2026-12-10",
  "end_date": "2026-12-15",
  "bounding_box": {
    "min_lat": 47.46,
    "max_lat": 47.54,
    "min_lon": 19.01,
    "max_lon": 19.10
  },
  "file_manifest": {
    "itinerary.json": { "sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855", "size_bytes": 14205 },
    "wallet.json": { "sha256": "...", "size_bytes": 3512 },
    "expenses.json": { "sha256": "...", "size_bytes": 2810 },
    "collections.json": { "sha256": "...", "size_bytes": 1104 }
  }
}

docs.title: 2.4 Domain Payloads
docs.text:
1. itinerary.json:
  2. trip_id, destination, days_count.
  3. days: list of day objects with date, day number, and chronological slots.
  4. slots: time windows, activity details, POI coordinates (lat, lon), category, estimated duration, cost, notes.
  5. routes: Valhalla route geometries (GeoJSON LineString or encoded polyline6), travel mode (walk, transit, bicycle), step maneuvers, and transit line details.

  6. travel_constraints: pace, user tastes, tag affinities at generation time.

  7. wallet.json:

  8. tickets: list of tickets (type: flight, train, bus, lodging, event, attraction).
  9. booking_anchors: flight segments (IATA codes, carriers, flight numbers, departure/arrival times, seats) and hotel anchors (check-in/out, address).
  10. barcodes: format (QR_CODE, AZTEC, PDF_417, CODE_128), raw decoded payload string.

  11. attachments: list of files in attachments/tickets/ associated with each ticket.

  12. expenses.json:

  13. currency: default trip currency (e.g., EUR, USD).
  14. participants: list of traveler profiles (ID, display name, role).
  15. expenses: amount, payer ID, category, timestamp, description, split rules.

  16. settlement: net balance per participant, debt minimization transfer graph.

  17. collections.json:

  18. collections: user-curated place lists (e.g. "Rooftop Bars", "Specialty Coffee").
  19. items: place ID, title, notes, coordinates, visited status.
  20. notes: freeform markdown notes and packing list checklists.

docs.title: 3. Privacy & Export Profiles
docs.text:
The packager supports two export profiles:

  1. full_vault (Default):
  2. Complete 1:1 export for private backup or transferring between self-hosted instances.
  3. Includes full traveler PII (emails, names), expenses, PNR reservation codes, barcode payloads, and raw PDF/PKPass attachments.

  4. Supports optional AES-256 container encryption.

  5. community_shareable:

  6. Sanitized export for sharing with friends or publishing itineraries publicly.
  7. Stripped Data:
    • Participant emails and internal user IDs (anonymized to "Traveler 1", "Traveler 2").
    • Sensitive booking codes (airline PNRs, ticket confirmation numbers, barcode payloads).
    • Individual expense transactions and settlement debt calculations.
    • Raw ticket PDFs and boarding pass scans.
  8. Retained Data:
    • Complete itinerary schedule, POIs, coordinates, route polylines, and timing.
    • Hotel anchors and flight schedules (without booking codes).
    • Collections, packing checklists, and general travel notes.
    • Curated trip photos (with option to scrub EXIF GPS).

docs.title: 4. Backend Implementation Architecture
docs.text:
backend/app/trip_package/
├── __init__.py
├── schemas.py          # Pydantic models for package manifests and sub-files
├── sanitizer.py        # Filter pipeline for community_shareable profile
├── packager.py         # TripPackager service assembling ZIP archive & checksums
└── unpacker.py         # Package integrity and validation engine

docs.title: 4.1 Packaging Flow
docs.text:
1. Fetch TripModel with related participants, expenses, tickets, collections, and photos via SQLAlchemy async session.
  2. Construct structured domain dictionaries according to the .trip specification.
  3. If export_profile == "community_shareable", pass the payloads through TripSanitizer.
  4. Stream entries into a temporary ZIP container using zipfile.ZipFile:
  5. Store mimetype without compression at the beginning.
  6. Write itinerary.json, wallet.json, expenses.json, collections.json.
  7. Resolve and copy ticket attachments and photos into attachments/.
  8. Calculate SHA-256 for all members and write paladio.json.
  9. Stream the resulting file via GET /api/trips/{trip_id}/export.

docs.title: 4.2 Security & Safety Guardrails
docs.text:
• Zip-Slip Protection: When reading/unpacking, validate all member paths using os.path.commonpath to prevent path traversal.
  • Resource Limits: Enforce maximum uncompressed size and file count checks to protect against zip bombs.
  • Dynamic Data Integrity: All data is populated dynamically from PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Automated Tests (backend/tests/test_trip_package.py)
docs.text:
• Test package creation for a trip with full attachments, tickets, expenses, and itinerary data.
  • Validate ZIP container structure and mimetype location.
  • Verify SHA-256 checksums in paladio.json match file contents.
  • Verify community_shareable sanitization (no PNRs, no emails, no debt amounts).
  • Verify export API endpoint returns valid file with correct headers.

docs.title: 1. Overview & Motivation
docs.text: The configuration workstation (/config) was recently extracted from a monolithic page into modular subcomponents, but the category taxonomy and card layouts still suffer from structural friction: 1. Asymmetric & Fragmented Taxonomy: Regional & Currency exists as an orphaned single-item category, while Language & Locales is placed under Workspace & Interface. Meanwhile, personal profile settings and administrative user provisioning are mixed together under Governance & Security. 2. Missing Travel & Engine Domain Representation: As a sovereign travel intelligence platform powered by LangGraph multi-agent swarms, deterministic C++20 combinatorial routing, and continuous ML taste learning, settings for solver constraints, map cartography, agent critic behaviors, units of measurement, and data vault backups have had no formal persistence layer or UI home. 3. Card Presentation Upgrade: Settings cards need to transition to a modern, tactile card archetype inspired by the user-provided reference design (clean outer cards, segmented sub-tab pills, nested tactical panels with rounded controls, toggle switches, and 3-dot contextual action menus) fully unified with Paladio's Pacific Jazz & Japanese Minimalist Tactical aesthetic. 4. Unified Backend Persistence: Both user-level travel preferences and instance-level system configurations must be persisted cleanly without mock fallbacks: - Personal travel settings (maps, units, solver_preferences) persist to UserModel.preferences (JSONB) via PATCH /users/me. - Instance/admin settings (engine, swarm, vault) persist to SystemConfigModel (system_config table) via typed GET/POST /system/settings/{domain} endpoints with strict Pydantic validation.

docs.title: First Autonomous Swarm Trip
docs.text: In this tutorial, you will plan a trip using Paladio's Active Engine cockpit (/engine), configure travel constraints and anchors, stream real-time WebSocket telemetry from the multi-agent swarm, and inspect the converged combinatorial itinerary.

docs.title: 1. Navigating to the Active Engine Cockpit
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to: 

http://localhost:3000/engine
Or click Active Engine in the sidebar navigation.

The Active Engine interface is structured into two main workspaces: - 01 // MISSION PREPARATION: Configuration interface for prompt intent, budget, meal windows, and flight/hotel anchors. - 02 // TELEMETRY CONSOLE: Live streaming terminal and output panel (OUTPUT TELEMETRY) powered by persistent WebSockets.

docs.title: 2. Configuring the Travel Parameters (01 // MISSION PREPARATION)
docs.text: In the Mission Preparation tab, set up your trip parameters:

docs.title: Step 2.1: Trip Intent & Preferences
docs.text:
In the > TRIP INTENT & PREFERENCES textarea, define your qualitative travel goals:

"Visit the main cultural landmarks and museums. Love traditional bistros and relaxed cafes."

This prompt is analyzed by the sovereign local LLM (prompt_analyzer) to update your continuous 768-D taste vector and extract domain category affinities.

docs.title: Step 2.2: Financial Budget Ceiling
docs.text:
In > BUDGET CEILING, enter your currency envelope: 

$ 1500 USD
The C++ solver uses this constraint to enforce a strict upper bound on POI admission fees and transit legs.

docs.title: Step 2.3: Mandatory Meal Windows
docs.text:
Under > MEAL CONSTRAINTS, review the culturally calibrated meal windows: - Breakfast: 08:00 \(\rightarrow\) 10:00 - Lunch: 12:00 \(\rightarrow\) 14:30 - Dinner: 19:30 \(\rightarrow\) 22:00

You can click + ADD MEAL WINDOW (e.g., for an afternoon snack) or adjust the boundary hours. The solver treats these as hard temporal time windows where food venues must be scheduled.

docs.title: Step 2.4: Travel Anchors (Flights & Hotel)
docs.text:
Paladio anchors itineraries around real flight arrival/departure times and lodging locations. Select your mode:

  • Simulated Anchors (Test Mode):
  • Origin City: Madrid
  • Destination City: Paris
  • Automated Generation: Generates round-trip flight bookings between real IATA airports (MAD \(\rightarrow\) CDG) and verifies a hotel in the destination city for 5 days.
  • Direct Ticket Ingestion (Production Mode):
  • Paste raw flight confirmation text, boarding passes, or hotel vouchers directly into the intake box for deterministic parsing by the Pydantic AI ticket_parser agent.

docs.title: 3. Initializing the Solver & Streaming Telemetry
docs.text:
Click the blue INITIALIZE SOLVER [MADRID -> PARIS] button at the bottom of the form.

The interface immediately switches to 02 // TELEMETRY CONSOLE and the OUTPUT TELEMETRY panel connects via WebSockets (/api/v1/ws/stream):

[PHASE: PARSER]      Extracting booking anchors...
                     -> Origin: Madrid (MAD) | Destination: Paris (CDG)
                     -> Hotel: Hotel Pullman Paris Tour Eiffel
                     -> Dates: 5-day optimization horizon
[PHASE: CONSTRAINTS] Deterministically assembling temporal & financial bounds...
                     -> Budget: $1500.00 USD
                     -> Hard Meal Windows: 3 daily (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner)
[PHASE: ANALYSIS]    Extracting travel tastes & tag affinities via Ollama...
                     -> High Affinities: art_culture (0.92), food_culinary (0.88)
[PHASE: ML_SCORING]  Batch encoding POIs into 16-D feature tensors...
                     -> Computing Bayesian smoothed ratings
                     -> Applying user taste EMA vector update
[PHASE: SOLVER]      Dispatching to C++ paladio-core branch-and-bound solver...
                     -> Evaluated 3,840 graph permutations in 1.86 ms
[PHASE: COMPLETED]   Optimal multi-day itinerary converged!

docs.title: 4. Inspecting and Saving the Results
docs.text: Once converged, the interface renders the interactive results in the right viewport:

docs.title: 1. The Daily Trip Timeline (TripTimeline)
docs.text:
• Day-by-Day Tabs: Navigate through each scheduled day.
  • Chronological Time Cards: Fixed POI visit windows (\([09:30, 11:30]\)) displaying attraction names, estimated admission costs, and categories.
  • Dedicated Meal Blocks: Culturally scheduled lunch and dinner venues.
  • Multimodal Transit Buffers: Walking and metro transit times with live fare estimates calculated between consecutive POIs.

docs.title: 2. Saving to Vault & Upcoming Trips
docs.text: Click the SAVE TRIP TO VAULT button in the header of the converged itinerary: - The itinerary is permanently saved to PostgreSQL. - You can now view and manage it under Upcoming Trips (/trips) and explore historical itineraries in the Itinerary Vault (/vault).

docs.title: 5. What Just Happened Under the Hood?
docs.text:
1. ticket_parser Agent: Verified flight timings and hotel check-in/out bounds using Pydantic AI models.
  2. assemble_constraints_node: Synthesized financial envelopes, meal windows, and spatial anchors into a validated TravelConstraints structure.
  3. prompt_analyzer Agent: Extracted semantic tastes and executed an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) update on your permanent 768-D latent vector.
  4. MLScorer: Encoded POIs in the destination city into 16-D tensors, computing Bayesian-smoothed multi-attribute utility scores.
  5. paladio-core (C++): Formulated and solved the Time-Constrained Orienteering Problem with Time Windows (TCOPTW) via branch-and-bound DFS and Knapsack bounding in sub-millisecond time.

Congratulations! You have completed your first autonomous swarm-optimized trip with Paladio.

docs.title: Quickstart with Docker
docs.text: In this 5-minute tutorial, you will launch the complete Paladio ecosystem locally using Docker Compose. Zero cloud subscriptions or external API keys are required.

docs.title: 1. System Requirements
docs.text: Before starting, ensure your system has: - Operating System: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora), macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel), or Windows (via WSL2). - Docker & Compose: Docker Engine 24.0+ and Docker Compose v2+. - RAM: Minimum 8 GB (16 GB recommended for concurrent local LLM inference). - Disk Space: ~10 GB free space for database storage and quantized model weights.

docs.title: 2. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the Paladio monorepo and navigate to its root:

git clone https://github.com/Leandro-Juan/Paladio.git
cd Paladio

docs.title: 3. Environment Configuration
docs.text:
Paladio uses standard 12-factor configuration via .env. A complete local development template is provided:

cp .env.example .env

The default .env is pre-configured to communicate seamlessly across the Docker network: - POSTGRES_HOST=postgres - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0 - FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH=/opt/models/fastembed

docs.title: 4. Spin Up the Stack
docs.text:
Launch the container cluster in detached mode:

docker compose up -d

Docker will start the following coordinated services: 1. postgres: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector and TimescaleDB extensions. 2. redis: Redis 7 for task queuing, caching, and LangGraph checkpointer persistence. 3. backend: FastAPI Semantic Gateway, Celery worker threads, and in-process CPU ONNX embeddings (fastembed nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5-Q baked into the image). 4. frontend: Next.js web client with interactive maps and telemetry.

Verify that all containers are healthy:

docker compose ps

docs.title: 5. Verify the Installation
docs.text:
Once the containers are running, access the user-facing endpoints:

Service Local URL Description Next.js Web UI http://localhost:3000 Interactive dashboard, trip timeline, and affinity radar FastAPI Swagger Docs http://localhost:8000/docs REST API exploration and schema definitions WebSocket Gateway ws://localhost:8000/ws/stream Real-time bi-directional agent streaming endpoint

docs.title: 6. Next Steps
docs.text: Now that your sovereign stack is operational, proceed to the First Autonomous Swarm Trip tutorial to generate your first optimized itinerary.
